content_of_post_to_comment: The classic statement of the French new left, “under the cobblestone, the beach,” has always irritated me. It presents primitivism as pure play and enjoyment; if we could just “get back” before the cobblestones were laid, we could live authentic, playful, and carefree lives. But castaways starve to death on beaches. They (like the “tropical paradises” of South Sea islands) are in reality deeply unforgiving environments. Those primitivists (and they come in both left- and right-wing variants) who rail against “the system” don’t seem to appreciate that “the system” is what is keeping the gigantic populations of the 21st century alive. Strip away “the cobblestones” and there would be the greatest die off in human history. Perhaps this is what they want.
comment: The overlooked distinction may be between rejecting civilization and rejecting its costs. Many critiques target the cobblestones, but the real question is whether we can redesign them without pretending the beach was ever benign.
